narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year, which is low but enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this decision were your number of past class failures, whether you receive extra educational support at school, and your desire to pursue higher education. These stood out above everything else in your profile, including your family background, study habits, and social life.

Having no previous failures worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing. However, the model noted that you are not currently receiving any extra educational support from the school—something that the vast majority of students who ultimately pass also do not receive, but which in your specific combination of circumstances became an important missing piece. Most importantly, although you have a clear ambition to continue into higher education (a goal shared by every student who passed), the model still saw this as contributing to a small increase in risk when combined with the other factors.

To improve, you should seriously consider accepting the remedial courses now being offered. They can fill the support gap the model identified, help maintain your clean record of no past failures, and strengthen your path toward the higher education you clearly want. Taking this step early gives you the best chance of turning that 10% risk into a confident pass. (218 words)
